## constitution-check

### Contract Emission Without API Credentials

Scenarios:
- Contract emitted with no credential present
- Machine-readable contract via --json
- Nonexistent change fails with a clear error, not an auth error

### No Direct AI Provider Invocation

Scenarios:
- No provider client is constructed during contract emission
- No provider client is constructed during verdict recording
- Full check runs end-to-end with no credential in the environment

### Verdict Schema Validation

Scenarios:
- Malformed verdict is rejected without persisting anything
- Unparseable verdict input is rejected
- Well-formed empty verdict passes validation

### Verdict Recording and Blocking-Violation Exit Semantics

Scenarios:
- Verdict with no blocking violations exits 0
- Critical violation is always blocking
- Unjustified major violation is blocking
- Justified major violation is not blocking

### Violations Report Format and Location Preserved

Scenarios:
- Clean verdict produces the no-violations report
- Violations report renders each violation with its fields

### Skill-Driven Two-Step Check Flow

Scenarios:
- Skill completes a full check with no manual workaround
- Skill surfaces a blocking result rather than masking it
- Skill template and deployed copy stay byte-identical

### Idempotent Re-Check Replaces the Prior Verdict

Scenarios:
- Re-running the check overwrites the prior report
- Re-running with an unchanged clean verdict still overwrites

## Context Engine — Specification

## Finalize and Ship

### Spec Delta Merge

Scenarios:
- New capability created from a confirmed ADDED delta
- Re-applying an ADDED delta does not duplicate an existing requirement
- ADDED idempotency holds without a base_versions entry

### Finalizer Orchestration

Scenarios:
- Incomplete artifact blocks finalize before gates or merge run
- Gate failure leaves the target capability spec untouched
- Retry after a fixed gate applies the merge exactly once

### Merge Safety Pipeline

Scenarios:
- Successful merge
- Dry-run skips git writes
- Conflict detected
- Base drift does not block merge

### Finalize Lock Contention Error Message

Scenarios:
- Lock held by a live process recommends a retry, not manual deletion
- Re-running finalize reclaims a dead-pid lock without manual cleanup

### Finalize Lock Staleness Fallback Via Mtime

Scenarios:
- Ambiguous pid liveness with an expired mtime is reclaimed
- Fresh lock with a confirmed live owner is respected
- Dead-pid reclaim path is preserved alongside the mtime fallback

### Stale Finalize Lock Surfaced In Status

Scenarios:
- Status reports a detected stale lock
- Status is unchanged when no stale lock is present

### Stale Finalize Lock Surfaced In Next Routing

Scenarios:
- Next surfaces the stale lock instead of routing into a failing finalize
- Next routing is unchanged when no stale lock is present

### Explicit Capability Target Selection In Spec Authoring

Scenarios:
- Instructions surface existing capabilities before authoring
- Generated scaffold carries an explicit target field, not an implicit slug default

### Merge Target Confirmation At Completion

Scenarios:
- Unconfirmed self-slug target is refused
- Explicit new-capability marker allows completion
- Non-ADDED operations against a nonexistent capability still hard-fail

### Trivial Workflow Verification Artifact Contract Agreement

Scenarios:
- Declared contract and instructed behavior agree
- Following instructions lets completion succeed
- Finalize completeness gate passes without manual patching

## fix-gate-infrastructure-bundle

### Gate execution MUST honor all three `on_failure` policies uniformly

Scenarios:
- retry_once retries on first fail
- retry_once does not retry on initial pass
- continue_with_warning downgrades fail to warn
- stop on fail causes remaining gates to be skipped
- stop does not affect gates earlier in the batch

### Gate `warn` status MUST be treated as pass across CLI commands

Scenarios:
- verify exits 0 when a gate returns warn
- verify exits non-zero when any gate returns fail
- finalize accepts warn results

### Workflow YAMLs MUST NOT reference unimplemented gates

Scenarios:
- standard.yaml does not reference unimplemented gates
- full.yaml does not reference unimplemented gates
- quick.yaml does not reference unimplemented gates

### GateRegistry tests MUST cover each policy branch

Scenarios:
- test suite asserts each on_failure branch

## instruction-contracts

### Persona Text Is Derived At Runtime From The Agent Definition

Scenarios:
- Editing an agent definition file changes the emitted persona
- No persona string literals remain in the instruction-generating source

### Every Referenced Agent Name Resolves To An Existing Agent Definition

Scenarios:
- All agent references across shipped workflows resolve
- A newly introduced agent reference without a definition file is detectable

### Agent Resolution Failure Fails Loudly, Never Silently Substitutes

Scenarios:
- Unresolvable agent name produces a named error instead of a fallback persona
- A resolvable agent name never triggers the failure path

### Agent Aliases Are Explicit And Resolve To The Real Agent's Identity

Scenarios:
- A declared alias resolves to its mapped agent's own persona
- An undeclared name is never treated as an implicit alias

### Emitted Instructions Contract Carries Complete Agent Identity

Scenarios:
- Instructions output includes name, persona, and tools sourced from the same definition
- A tool list change in the agent definition is reflected in the next generation

### Source And Deployed Agent Definitions Remain Byte-Identical

Scenarios:
- Source and deployed agent definitions match after an edit
- A divergence between source and deployed copies is detectable

## orchestration-guard

### Inline Command-Text Tokens Never Authorize a Blocked Subcommand

Scenarios:
- A bare inline token with no external signal is rejected
- No code path treats inline command text as sufficient on its own

### Fork-Dispatched Subcommands Require Verified Caller Identity

Scenarios:
- Fork-dispatched subcommand with verified caller identity is accepted
- Fork-dispatched subcommand without verified caller identity is rejected

### Main-Session Lifecycle Subcommands Require a Non-Forgeable Session Credential

Scenarios:
- Sanctioned skill-driven call with a valid credential is accepted
- Expired, out-of-scope, or malformed credential is rejected
- Credential forgery requires an audit-visible act outside command text
- No credential present is rejected with skill guidance

### Unrecognized metta Subcommands Fail Closed

Scenarios:
- An unrecognized subcommand is blocked, not silently allowed
- A newly added unknown subcommand does not silently pass until classified

### Every Rejection and Every Tier-2 Acceptance Is Recorded

Scenarios:
- A session-tier rejection is recorded with tier and reason
- A session-tier acceptance is recorded
- A fork-tier rejection is recorded with tier and reason

### Skill Contracts Reference Only the Sanctioned Authorization Mechanism

Scenarios:
- No skill contract instructs typing a self-authored token
- A newly added skill contract that reintroduces a self-authored token is a detectable violation

### Forked Agents Are Blocked From Running Background Bash

Scenarios:
- Background Bash from a verified fork-tier caller is rejected
- Background Bash from a caller without verified fork identity is unaffected by this rule

### The Trust Model Is Documented Where Operators and Contributors Will Read It

Scenarios:
- Header documentation describes both tiers and the emergency bypass
- Generated workflow guidance matches the documented model

## fix-metta-propose-has-no-flag-stop-after-planning-artifacts

### `metta propose` MUST accept a `--stop-after <artifact>` option

Scenarios:
- option appears in CLI help
- option is accepted with a valid value
- option is omitted, full-lifecycle behavior preserved

### `--stop-after` MUST be validated against the resolved workflow

Scenarios:
- unknown artifact id is rejected before any side effects
- execution-phase artifact id is rejected
- planning-phase id from a non-default workflow is accepted

### change-record schema MUST persist `stop_after` as an optional field

Scenarios:
- schema accepts records with `stop_after`
- schema accepts records without `stop_after`
- schema rejects non-string `stop_after`

### `ArtifactStore.createChange` MUST accept and persist a `stopAfter` argument

Scenarios:
- `createChange` writes `stop_after` when supplied
- `createChange` omits `stop_after` when not supplied

### propose skill MUST honor the `stop_after` boundary

Scenarios:
- skill parses and forwards `--stop-after` from `$ARGUMENTS`
- skill exits cleanly at the stop-after boundary for `tasks`
- skill exits cleanly at the stop-after boundary for `spec`
- skill behaves identically when no `stop_after` is set

### `metta status` MUST surface `stop_after` in JSON output

Scenarios:
- `metta status --json` reflects `stop_after` when set
- `metta status --json` omits or nulls `stop_after` when not set

### `--stop-after` MUST compose with all existing propose flags

Scenarios:
- `--stop-after` composes with `--workflow` and `--auto`
- `--stop-after` composes with `--from-issue`

### handoff message MUST be deterministic and matchable

Scenarios:
- tests can assert the handoff line shape
- no implementation-implying lines appear
